mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 5 Series 545e engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used BMW 545e B58 engine typically costs £2,500-£4,500 depending on mileage and condition. A reconditioned unit ranges from £4,500-£6,500, while a fully rebuilt engine with warranty sits at £5,500-£8,000. Specialist fitting adds approximately £1,000-£1,600 in labour (14-18 hours at £65-£85/hr). Main dealer fitting costs 40-60% more, with some dealers quoting £14,000-£18,000 for a complete engine replacement.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of hybrid battery failure in a BMW 545e?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 545e's 11.6-12 kWh lithium-ion battery typically degrades over time. Early warning signs include reduced electric range (less than the original 33-35 miles), the engine engaging more frequently than expected, slight hesitation during acceleration, and cooling fans running longer after shutdown. Warning lights on the dashboard may indicate battery management system faults.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 5 Series 545e?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends entirely on the car's condition and value. A G30 545e (2020-2023) typically holds £18,000-£35,000 value depending on mileage and specification. A rebuilt B58 engine at £5,500-£8,000 is typically justifiable if the car is otherwise well-maintained. However, if the car has significant body damage, suspension issues, or a degraded hybrid battery requiring replacement, evaluate the total repair cost against the vehicle's value.

mainEntity.name: What engine does the BMW 545e use?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 545e uses the B58B30M1 (also known as B58X) - a 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-six petrol engine producing 286hp (210 kW), combined with an electric motor producing 109hp. Total system output is 394hp (290 kW) and 600Nm (442 lb-ft) of torque. The electric motor is integrated into the ZF 8-speed automatic gearbox. The battery capacity is 11.6-12 kWh, offering a WLTP electric range of 54-57 km (33-35 miles).

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 5 Series 545e engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 545e engine replacement takes 4-8 days from booking to collection, depending on parts availability and workshop workload. The B58 is a common engine, but the hybrid system adds complexity - sourcing a quality rebuilt or reconditioned unit may take 3-5 days. Supply and fit through our network typically completes within 5-8 working days.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a BMW 545e replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Rebuilt and reconditioned B58 engines typically include full parts and labour cover; used engines usually carry a 3-6 month warranty depending on the supplier. Always confirm that the hybrid system components (electric motor, battery management system) are covered under the warranty terms if they are affected by the engine replacement.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 5 Series 545e - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 545e was introduced as part of the G30 5 Series facelift (LCI) in 2020, bringing the brand's flagship six-cylinder plug-in hybrid powertrain to the 5 Series range. Positioned above the four-cylinder 530e, the 545e combined the acclaimed B58 3.0-litre turbocharged petrol engine with an electric motor to deliver near-M5 performance with plug-in efficiency.

milestones.description: B58B30M1, 3.0L turbocharged inline-six petrol + electric motor, 394hp system output - G30 LCI 545e xDrive launched as the flagship PHEV in the 5 Series range

commonProblems.h2: BMW 5 Series 545e Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 545e's B58 engine is one of BMW's most celebrated modern powertrains - smooth, responsive and generally robust. However, the added complexity of the plug-in hybrid system introduces additional potential failure points. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Electric Water Pump Failure - The B58's Most Common Weakness
problems.rootCause: Like earlier N-series BMW engines, the B58 uses an electric water pump. The pump's electronics and bearing assembly can fail, causing intermittent or complete coolant flow loss - often without warning until the engine enters limp mode or overheats.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electric water pump and thermostat; coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: Best option if caught before overheating
Only if overheating has caused head gasket or bottom-end damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical G30 545e (2020-2023) holds £18,000-£35,000 value depending on mileage and specification. Water pump replacement at specialist rates (£500-£900) is a fraction of the car's value. A full rebuilt engine replacement is viable on higher-value examples but should be carefully evaluated against the car's overall condition.
problems.recommendation: Replace the water pump and thermostat preventatively at 70k-80k miles if you plan to keep the car. This is the single most effective way to avoid catastrophic overheating on the B58.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B58B30M1 BMW 5 Series 545e engine prices

problems.group: Hybrid Battery Degradation & High-Voltage System Issues
problems.h4: Hybrid Battery Degradation & High-Voltage System Issues
problems.rootCause: The 545e's 11.6-12 kWh lithium-ion batterydegrades over time, reducing electric range from the original 33-35 miles (WLTP)to significantly less. Battery management system (BMS) faults can trigger warning lights and, in severe cases, prevent the car from starting or running in hybrid mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed cells or modules; BMS recalibration
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if only part of the pack has failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete battery pack replacement; system coding
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if battery is heavily degraded
Only if battery failure has caused collateral damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a 545e worth £18,000-£35,000, full battery replacement at £4,000-£7,000 is a significant but justifiable investment if the car is otherwise well-maintained. On lower-value examples (sub-£15,000), evaluate carefully against the car's overall condition.
problems.recommendation: Monitor electric range regularly - a gradual decline is normal, but a sudden drop indicates a cell or module failure. Have the battery health checked by a BMW hybrid specialist before committing to replacement. Partial module replacement is often more cost-effective than a full pack replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt BMW 5 Series 545e engine prices

problems.group: Cooling System Leaks & PCV Valve Failure
problems.h4: Cooling System Leaks & PCV Valve Failure
problems.rootCause: The B58's cooling system uses plastic components (expansion tank, coolant pipes) that can become brittle and crack over time. The PCV (positive crankcase ventilation) valve is integrated into the valve cover and can fail, causing rough idle, oil consumption and, in severe cases, increased crankcase pressure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cracked plastic components; coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: Viable; use upgraded aluminium parts where available
Only if PCV failure has caused oil starvation or bottom-end damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: These repairs are well within the value of most 545e examples. The PCV valve is the more critical of the two - failure can lead to oil consumption and, in extreme cases, engine damage.
problems.recommendation: Inspect cooling system components at every service - small cracks can be spotted before they fail. If you notice rough idle or increased oil consumption, have the PCV system checked immediately. Replacing the valve cover proactively is cheaper than a new engine.
